headline: Silver and black every day, Fiesta color for the occasion: win San Antonio through its West Side makers and its April.
thesis: San Antonio is a one-team city where silver and black is civic dress worn by abuelas, Joint Base San Antonio families and Laredo road-trippers alike, and the Duncan-Popovich habit of restraint is something fans actively guard. Its color lives in a different register: Fiesta's papel picado pink, turquoise and marigold, the medal-pin habit, and a West Side hand-made tradition of sign-painter lettering, Chicano screenprint, conjunto posters and lowrider pinstripe. Nike wins by keeping core product monochrome and precise, then spending color only on occasions the city already keeps (the returning Fiesta-stripe City Edition, an early-April Fiesta and playoff drop, a February rodeo crossover), made with credited, paid local artists. The money is in tiering for a price-aware, family-sized, bilingual region, with a Wembanyama youth ladder doing the heavy lifting.

archetype.name: The Civic Family Contender
archetype.description: A multigenerational, majority-Latino, military-heavy fan base that treats the Spurs as the city's shared family table, prizes humility over flash, and now expects a title after losing the 2026 Finals.

pulse.teamMoment: The 2026 West champions (62-20, beat OKC 4-3 in the West finals) lost the Finals 4-1 to the Knicks, then extended Wembanyama (5 years, $252M) and Fox (through 2029-30) and run the core back under Mitch Johnson as title co-favorites with OKC. Opening night is the Oct 20 West finals rematch with OKC, and the Knicks come back on Christmas Day (at MSG) and Mar 7 (in San Antonio).
pulse.sentiment: Confident and hungry rather than celebratory: proud of the West title, stung by the Knicks, protective of Spurs humility, and watching Project Marvel and the Frost Bank Center lease talks with civic interest but not alarm.

topInsights.title: Fiesta is the city's design system, and it lands on the first round
topInsights.insight: Fiesta's ten days in the second half of April (Battle of Flowers, Fiesta Flambeau, NIOSA at La Villita) overlap the first playoff round, and its medal culture means locals already treat a hat or sash as a surface to layer collectible pins on. Fans embraced the Fiesta-stripe City Edition because it abstracts that palette into stripes on black instead of costume.
topInsights.implication: Make April the market's biggest product moment: an early-April drop keyed to the returning City Edition stripes, plus a medal-style pin and patch system fans can layer, licensed through the Fiesta organizations where the name or medal designs appear.

topInsights.title: Restraint is the brand; color is the occasion
topInsights.insight: Thirty years of silver, black and white under Duncan and Popovich made understatement a civic value, and Spurs gear is worn in every month, not just game nights. The warmest nostalgia attaches to the 1989-2002 teal, orange and fuchsia Fiesta era, but fans want it as an accent on black, not a takeover.
topInsights.implication: Keep core product tonal and monochrome with small, precise local details (woven labels, bilingual hang tags), and spend loud color only on City Edition, Fiesta and capsule drops.

topInsights.title: The hand-made city is the untold design story
topInsights.insight: San Antonio's visual voice is hand-made: sign-painter block capitals on taquerias, panaderias and tire shops, flat-color Chicano screenprint from the Guadalupe Cultural Arts Center lineage, Tejano gig-poster type, papel picado cutwork and lowrider pinstripe and candy paint. None of it has carried a Spurs uniform, and the Fiesta stripe has.
topInsights.implication: Commission local letterers, printmakers and pinstripers for artist-credited graphics now, and use the hand-lettered West Side as the next City Edition story once the Fiesta stripe has run its two seasons.

topInsights.title: Taste is set on the West Side; volume runs through malls and Academy
topInsights.insight: Cultural credibility comes from the West Side, Market Square and the Southtown and Blue Star scene, while volume flows through North Star, La Cantera, Ingram Park and South Park mall chains, Academy, Dick's and the Frost Bank Center team store. Independent sneaker culture is thinner than in Houston or Dallas.
topInsights.implication: Seed artist drops in community pop-ups (Guadalupe, First Fridays, Ingram Park) first, then scale the stripe and core product through allocation and shop-in-shop quality at the volume doors rather than building a flagship.

topInsights.title: Tier for the family of four, the E-5 and the Alamo Heights collector
topInsights.insight: This is a price-aware market with spend clustered on the Texas August sales-tax holiday (items under $100), military 1st-and-15th paydays, Christmas and Las Posadas, and Fiesta, and with flea markets like Traders Village setting a bootleg price floor. Wembanyama is now the role model for a generation of local kids.
topInsights.implication: Build a clear ladder: a sub-$100 youth and tee tier ready before the August holiday, swingman as the committed buy, and protected authentic and limited drops; never chase flea-market prices with the top tier.

topInsights.title: Spurs Nation is a region, a border and now a global audience
topInsights.insight: The fan base runs to Laredo, Corpus Christi, the Rio Grande Valley and Monterrey, and Mexican shoppers drive to La Cantera, North Star and the San Marcos outlets around Buen Fin and the December holidays. Ginobili's Latin American following and Wembanyama's French one, plus games in Austin, Paris and Manchester, make the team travel.
topInsights.implication: Make bilingual, Spanish-first copy the default on local drops, align November promos with Buen Fin, and run a clean black-and-silver travel story for the international games.

topInsights.title: Hunger, not a parade
topInsights.insight: Fans read the Finals loss to the Knicks as chapter one of a Wembanyama-Fox-Castle-Harper window, with OKC the red-hot rival and two Knicks rematches on the calendar. The Project Marvel arena plan and lease talks are a live civic topic with public-money sensitivities.
topInsights.implication: Write forward-looking, earned messaging for Oct 20, Dec 25 and Mar 7, avoid anything that reads as commemorating a title that did not happen, and keep downtown-arena and skyline nostalgia off product.

collection.name: Puro SA
collection.story: San Antonio dresses in silver and black every day and in Fiesta color when the city celebrates. Puro SA keeps those two registers separate: a precise monochrome core, a Fiesta season that layers like medals, and a hand-made West Side line drawn by the city's own letterers and printmakers.

uniform.narrative: For the City Edition after the Fiesta stripe's run, tell the story every San Antonio kid grew up reading: the hand-painted letters on taquerias, panaderias, tire shops and conjunto dance posters across the West and South Sides. It honors the city's makers instead of its postcards, and it reads as nobody but San Antonio.
motifs: Sign-painter outlined block capitals with drop shadow
uniform.typography: A hand-lettered 'San Antonio' chest script and matching numbers commissioned from a West Side sign painter, outlined in silver with a candy-red drop shadow; credit the letterer on the jock tag.
details: Waistband in talavera-tile geometry in cobalt on cream
Neck tape with an abstracted accordion-bellows line pattern developed with a conjunto musician or the Guadalupe Cultural Arts Center
Jock tag reading 'Hecho a mano en San Antonio' with the letterer's name
Side panel pinstripe scroll drawn by a local pinstriper
Court tie-in: hand-lettered baseline wordmark painted live by the commissioned artist
avoid: Repeating the Fiesta stripe or its black base, which is the City Edition for 2025-26 and 2026-27
The Alamo, mission church interiors and other sacred or contested sites as graphics
Dia de los Muertos calaveras, sombreros, mustaches or Mexican-flag shorthand
Copying any real business's sign or a lowrider club's plaque instead of commissioning original lettering

risks.risk: Fiesta name, medals and official art are controlled by local organizations, and Selena, H-E-B and Whataburger are tightly licensed.
risks.mitigation: Clear Fiesta use with the Fiesta San Antonio Commission before design lock, and use the stripe and medal form without the name if rights are not granted.

risks.risk: Lifting Mexican-American culture (Dia de los Muertos imagery, lowrider club plaques, papel picado art, the Alamo) would be read as appropriation in a city that guards it.
risks.mitigation: Commission, credit and pay San Antonio artists for every cultural cue, run designs past the Guadalupe Cultural Arts Center, and keep sacred and contested imagery off product.

risks.risk: Playoff disappointment or premature celebration after a Finals loss could sour the April drop.
risks.mitigation: Build the Fiesta capsule to sell as a city moment, not a title moment, and hold champion product until it is earned.

risks.risk: Flea-market and bootleg goods at Traders Village set a low price anchor in a price-aware market.
risks.mitigation: Win entry with a real sub-$100 tier and artist credibility rather than discounting the authentic top tier.

risks.risk: Project Marvel and lease politics make arena and downtown imagery sensitive.
risks.mitigation: Keep arena-move and skyline nostalgia off product and frame the story by neighborhood.

scorecard.rationale: A title co-favorite led by Nike's Wembanyama, in a one-team region that runs to Mexico, with some of the league's most specific design material (Fiesta, West Side craft, conjunto), puts opportunity, culture and fandom well above average. Retail is ordinary: mall, Academy and arena-store volume in a price-aware market with a thin independent sneaker scene and a real bootleg channel.
